title: 🏛️ Exam 2021 · writing prepared: a family birthday party ⭐⭐

questions.prompt: (Exam 2021) Task: "Today is your birthday. You are having a small family party. Write an e-mail to your English friend to tell her: what do you wear, what do you eat and drink, what do you do at the party, what presents do you get." The e-mail goes to Patricia, with the subject "My birthday party". What is the aim of the e-mail?

options.text: To invite Patricia to a birthday party that will take place at my house next week.
To tell Patricia about my birthday party: clothes, food, games and presents.
To thank Patricia for the birthday present that she sent me.
To ask Patricia about the clothes that she wears at her party.

questions.explanation: The task asks for four pieces of news about the party that is happening today: what is worn, what is eaten and drunk, what is done and what presents are received. The e-mail does not invite Patricia to a later party, does not thank her for a present and does not ask her about her own party.

questions.prompt: (Exam 2021) The questions of the task are in the present simple (What presents do you get?), so Sami answers in the present simple. Which sentence about the presents is correct?

options.text: My mother give me a book and my father give me a bike.
My mother gives me a book and my father give me a bike.
My mother gives me a book and my father gives me a bike.
My mother gives me a book and my father gives me a bike yesterday.

questions.explanation: The e-mail speaks about today, so the verb stays in the present simple, and with my mother or my father it takes -s: gives. Without the -s the verb does not agree with a singular subject, and a word like yesterday points to a past time, which has no place in a message about today.

questions.prompt: (Exam 2021) Sami must answer the four questions of the task. Match each question with the sentence of his e-mail that answers it.

options.text: What do you wear?
What do you eat and drink?
What do you do at the party?
What presents do you get?
We play games and we sing Happy Birthday.
My aunt gives me a red shirt and my uncle gives me a bike.
We eat a big chocolate cake and we drink orange juice.
I wear my best red shirt and white shoes.

questions.explanation: The question about clothes is answered by what Sami wears, the question about food and drink by the cake and the juice, the question about the party by the games and the song, and the question about presents by what the family gives him. The red shirt appears twice, and only the verb tells whether it is worn or given.

questions.prompt: (Exam 2021) Sami wants to use words of a party in his e-mail. Which of these words belong to a birthday party?

options.text: gift
stomachache
snacks
shopkeeper
crackers
balloons

questions.explanation: A gift, snacks, crackers and balloons all belong to a party, as the words of the unit say. A stomachache belongs to a visit to the doctor and a shopkeeper to a shop, not to a birthday party at home.

questions.prompt: (Exam 2021) Sami writes to his English friend Patricia and signs the e-mail with his own name. Which frame is correct?

options.text: The e-mail starts with "Dear Sami," and ends with "Yours, Sami".
The e-mail starts with "Dear Sami," and ends with "Yours, Patricia".
The e-mail starts with "Dear Patricia," and ends with "Yours, Sami".
The e-mail starts with "Dear Patricia," and ends with "Yours, Patricia".

questions.explanation: An e-mail to Patricia opens with Dear Patricia, and closes with Yours and the name of the writer, Sami. Writing to Sami, or signing with the name of the person who receives the message, puts the two people the wrong way round.

questions.prompt: (Exam 2021) In his e-mail, Sami has already written about his clothes, his food and drink, and his games. Which sentence can he add about the presents?

options.text: My school starts at eight o'clock every morning.
The bakery near our house sells good bread.
Last year I bought a perfume for my mother.
My cousin gives me a football and a card.

questions.explanation: A sentence that can join the e-mail must answer the question about the presents. The school timetable, the bakery and a gift bought for another person in another year do not tell what Sami gets on his own birthday, so they are off the subject even if they are true.
